 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 6639 of 2019  ==========================================================
 DILIPKUMAR MANUBHAI PATEL  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ORS.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR. BHAVIK P SHAH(6391) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR DAXAY D PATEL(6633) for the Respondent(s) No. 3  NOTICE SERVED BY DS for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR MANAN MEHTA APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================

sentences.text: Heard learned advocate for the respective parties.

2. The solitary contention raised by learned advocate for the petitioner is that FIR being I-CR No.4 of 2007 registered with Gayakwad Haveli Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 46 of the Banking Regulation Act on the allegation that accused with the connivance of each other obtained loan of Rs.2,48,50,000/- from the Bank by placing forged and fabricated documents.

He would further submit that out of 13 accused persons, two accused are expired and remaining accused persons have quashed the FIR on the basis of consent quashing proceedings recorded by this Hon'ble Court.
He would further submit that role of the petitioner is limited to the extent that petitioner issued valuation certificate for the properties which is put in the mortgage for obtaining loan.

He would Dilipkumar Manubhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161615798/
1 submit that role of the petitioner is lesser than the role of the main accused against whom the FIR came to be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6639/2019 ORDER DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined quashed by way of consent proceedings and therefore this petition may be allowed.
3.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the respondent no.3 would submit that when the FIR against the main accused is quashed in the consent quashing proceedings, the FIR against the petitioner may be quashed.
4. Learned APP submits to pass necessary order in the facts and circumstances of the case.

5. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the parties, what could be noticed that the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in SCR.A No.227 of 2012 has quashed the FIR in respect of co-accused person as per order order dated 29/03/2012; relevant paragraph thereof reads thus:
"2 This application under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 [for short, 'the Code'] is filed by the petitioners to quash the FIR being C.R. No.I4 of 2007 registered with Gaekwad Haveli Police Station, Ahmedabad, for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
420, 467,468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, on the ground that the amount borrowed from respondent No.2Bank and the outstanding dues of various loan accounts were fully paid up with interest by the petitioners.

That,even the nature of transaction if seen in the context of allegations, there was no intention on the part of the petitioners to commit offences as alleged and, on account of financial constrains at the relevant point of time, and upon realizing their mistake, now they have repaid the total amount of dues which is subject matter of the complaint qua them.
R/CR.MA/6639/2019 ORDER DATED:
The above aspect, namely, payment of outstanding dues in various loan accounts by the petitioners to respondent No.2Bank is verified by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2Bank.

The Liquidator of respondent No.2Bank, vide communication dated 27.3.2012, along with relevant statement of accounts, has Dilipkumar Manubhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161615798/
2 communicated to the learned counsel for respondent No.2Bank that the amount due in the loan accounts of the petitioners is paid up with interest and, accordingly, the outstanding dues of the petitioners are settled.

sentences.text: The communication dated 27.3.2012 is ordered to be taken on record.

Considering overall facts and circumstances of the case, in my view, the subject matter of the complaint is such for which no further proceedings are necessary and even financial aspect of the Bank is fully taken care of and protected and, therefore,
relegating the petitioners to undergo the rigors of trial would cause undue hardship and agony.
Hence, a case is made out to exercise powers under Section 482 of the Code to secure the ends of justice and, accordingly, the impugned complaint qua the petitioners is quashed and set aside.
The petition is allowed to the aforesaid extent.
Rule is made absolute.

Direct service is permitted."
6. To be noted further that, in respect of other co-accused the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in CR.MA No.15939 of 2011 has also quashed the FIR as per order dated 10/12/2013; relevant paragraph thereof reads thus:
"4.

The second respondent, an employee of the Textile Processors Co-operative Bank Limited, lodged the above referred first information report against the applicants herein alleging NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6639/2019 ORDER DATED:
12/03/2025 undefined commission of the offences punishable under sections 406,
420, 467, 468, 471 and 120 of the Indian Penal Code and section 46 of the Banking Regulations Act.

The allegations made in the complaint are to the effect that the applicants availed of huge loans from the bank on the basis of false documents and ultimately did not repay an amount of Rs.2,48,50,000/- with interest and accordingly committed the offence of section 406 IPC as well as other offences.

It appears that over a period of time, the applicants herein have repaid a substantial amount of Rs.2,10,65,438/- to the bank and amounts of Rs.12,90,877/- as well as Rs.10,94,423/- are still outstanding against which security deposits of Rs.72,02,342/-
are lying with the bank.

The Textile Processors Co-operative Bank Limited has been taken into liquidation and the Liquidator has, by a communication dated 5th December, 2013 addressed to the learned advocate for the third respondent, stated the aforesaid facts and has stated that the if the first information report in question is quashed, the bank is not likely to suffer any economic loss.
5.

Mr. M. Iqbal Shaikh, learned advocate for the applicants has submitted that in the light of the fact that the applicants have paid a substantial amount of the outstanding amount and in respect of the remaining amount, sufficient security deposits have been deposited, the bank has no objection if the first information report in question and all proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
Under the circumstances, no fruitful purpose would be served in prosecuting the applicants.
The first information report in question is, therefore, required to be quashed.

sentences.text: Mr. Dipen Dave, learned advocate for the third respondent - Liquidator has submitted that in the light of the fact that the outstanding amount due and payable to the bank has been paid and in respect of the remaining amount, there is more than sufficient security deposit lying with the bank, there cannot be any objection to the first information report being quashed."

7. Thus, when the role of the petitioner is much lessor than the role of the main accused against whom the FIR is already quashed and petitioner is shown as valuer as per charge-sheet papers, as also the loan amount is already secured as noted in the order passed by the co-ordinate Bench, the rolling over the FIR further into the trial would be nothing but a futile exercise.
8. For the foregoing reasons, the petition is allowed.
FIR being I-CR No.4 of 2007 registered with Gayakwad Haveli Police Station as well as consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof qua present petitioner is quashed and set aside.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
